solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Stingy individual used to be first to pay (4)

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

annotation.surface: A miser who once led the way in paying up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stingy' looks like mean with money; here it means having a sting, so the individual is an insect.
annotation.definitionFit: A wasp is a creature with a sting, so a stingy individual in the literal sense.

entries.clue: Beat offer to host Queen singer with cracking voice? (8)

indicators.note: BID holds R inside it, as a host holds a guest

blocks.note: a bid is an offer; it goes round R

annotation.surface: An offer made to have a hoarse Queen frontman perform, with a beat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Queen singer' suggests Freddie Mercury; Queen gives only R, and the singer is a bird. The whipbird is an Australian bird whose call ends in a sound like a whip crack.
annotation.definitionFit: The whipbird's song finishes with a loud crack, so it is a singer whose voice cracks.

entries.clue: Judgement’s epic settlement of considerable significance (8)

blocks.note: a saga is an epic tale
a city is a settlement of some size and status

annotation.surface: A verdict that an epic settlement of some case matters a great deal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' reads as a legal agreement beside 'Judgement'; it is a place where people settle, and the long tail pins it to a city rather than a village.
annotation.definitionFit: Sagacity is sound judgement, the quality of being wise.

entries.clue: Cook frequently repelled by religious leader’s salad? (6,4)

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so DO OFT is turned back to front

blocks.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader
to do food is to cook it

annotation.surface: A chef keeps being turned away by a rabbi, who wants his salad his own way.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as jokey: rabbit food is slang for salad, raw greens fit for a rabbit.
annotation.definitionFit: Rabbit food is a jokey name for salad and raw vegetables.

entries.clue: Time rejected article about conflict zone (5)

indicators.note: rejected = thrown back, so ERA is turned round
about = turned round, so AN is turned too

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

annotation.surface: A news story about a war zone gets spiked for lack of time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article AN.
annotation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of contest, originally where gladiators fought.

entries.clue: Doctor in cabal is connected to church (9)

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A physician who belongs to a secret clique turns out to have links to the church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' opens the clue as a person in the cabal; it is the verb. That makes 'is' look like the link, but it is part of the fodder, and 'is connected to church' is read with the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Basilican means relating to a basilica, a type of church.

entries.clue: Did career supply other use cases for property? (8,5)

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, in a pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order
the rearranged letters encase RACED

blocks.note: anagram of OTHER USE, split TER…HOUSE around RACED
to career is to rush along, so did career = raced

annotation.surface: A question about whether a working life produced other uses for a building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Career' is the verb, to go at speed, not a working life, and 'supply' is an adverb (in a supple way), not a verb or noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A terraced house, one of a row joined side by side, is a kind of property.

entries.clue: Unrequited love always behind novel (3-3)

indicators.note: behind = at the back, so AY is placed after NEW

blocks.note: ay (or aye) = always, an old word

annotation.surface: A heartbroken reader forever trailing after a romance novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unrequited love' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Unrequited' alone; 'love' is the O.
annotation.definitionFit: Unrequited feeling goes one way only, not returned.

entries.clue: Hopeless player joining band on keyboards (6)

indicators.note: the answer is formed where the words join together

annotation.surface: A useless musician is taken on as the band's keyboard player.
annotation.walkthrough: In British sport a donkey is a clumsy, hopeless player.
annotation.definitionFit: A donkey is British slang for an untalented player, especially in football.

entries.clue: Who doesn’t appreciate attempt to avoid usual price? (7)

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun 'one who doesn't appreciate'

indicators.note: GO is kept out of GOING RATE

blocks.note: the going rate is the usual price
a go = an attempt; it is removed

annotation.surface: A question about someone who doesn't value the effort to dodge paying the normal price.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue opens with a question as its definition: the answer is the person who doesn't appreciate.
annotation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, one who doesn't appreciate what is done for them.

entries.clue: Like particular books encapsulating author’s determination (13)

indicators.note: NT closes round ME like a capsule

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, books of the Bible

annotation.surface: A question of which books contain a writer's resolve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Determination' reads as resolve; here it means finding something out.
annotation.definitionFit: Ascertainment is the act of determining a fact, finding it out for certain.

entries.clue: Actor in theatre to increase performing (7)

annotation.surface: A stage actor whose part is growing while the show runs.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, where the surgeon is the one who acts.
annotation.definitionFit: A surgeon works in an operating theatre, so he is the one acting there.

entries.clue: Spooner’s excellent dance routine in pool (4,5)

indicators.note: Rev Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: crack = first-rate, as in 'crack troops'; it hands its CR to the next word and takes B
a ball is a formal dance; with CR in front it becomes CRAWL

annotation.surface: A fine dance number performed in a swimming pool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Routine' reads with 'dance' as a choreographed sequence; the definition is a swimming stroke.
annotation.definitionFit: Back crawl, or backstroke, is a stroke swum in the pool.

entries.clue: Saw commercial agency losing half its members (5)

indicators.note: AGENCY has six letters and loses three, leaving AGE

annotation.surface: An observer notes an advertising firm has cut half its staff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is a noun, an old saying.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: saw here is the old noun for a proverb or wise saying, unrelated to the tool.

entries.clue: Prerequisite for training when making a comeback? (6,6)

definitions.text: Prerequisite for training when making a comeback?

blocks.note: looks like sports preparation; it means what you need to travel by train
not an athlete's return to form but the journey back home

annotation.surface: An athlete asks what is needed to train for a comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Training' reads as sports practice; here it means travelling by train, and a return ticket is what you need to come back.
annotation.definitionFit: A return ticket lets you travel out by train and come back again.

entries.clue: Look like opinion having less sense lacks depth (4,5)

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so DAFTER goes without its D

blocks.note: your take on something is your opinion
d = depth, as in dimensions; it is removed

annotation.surface: A view that looks shallower and sillier than it should.
annotation.walkthrough: D for depth is the abbreviation used in measurements.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: children take after a parent when they inherit that parent's looks or manner.

entries.clue: Sailor and German soldier showing up everywhere (8)

indicators.note: German asks for the word before it in the German language, so 'and' becomes UND

annotation.surface: A sailor and a German soldier seem to turn up wherever you look.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a joining word, and 'German soldier' looks like one unit; 'German' works on 'and', and the soldier is an ant.
annotation.definitionFit: Something abundant is plentiful, found everywhere.

entries.clue: Better training drills ruled out (8)

indicators.note: to drill is to bore a hole into something, so PT bores into EXCEED

annotation.surface: Superior exercise routines were disallowed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drills' looks like a noun beside 'training'; it is the verb, with PT boring into EXCEED.
annotation.definitionFit: Excepted means left out, excluded, ruled out.

entries.clue: Give up television for emergent source of entertainment? (4-2-3-3)

blocks.note: to jack in is British slang for to quit

annotation.surface: Quit watching television in favour of some new kind of fun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Emergent' looks like new or rising; it is literal, the toy that springs up out of its box.
annotation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a toy whose figure pops out to amuse.

entries.clue: Two members of family tree (6)

blocks.note: a dam is a mother, usually of an animal

annotation.surface: Two relatives on a family tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Family tree' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'tree' alone. A dam is a mother, usually of an animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the damson is one kind of tree, a small plum.

entries.clue: Sweet note well conveyed by blessing (6)

indicators.note: NB is carried inside BOON

blocks.note: NB = nota bene, Latin for note well

annotation.surface: A sweet message, well received, carried along with a blessing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note well' is one unit, the Latin nota bene.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bonbon, from French bon, 'good', is a small sweet, often a chocolate.

entries.clue: American firm runs new plant to begin with (5)

annotation.surface: A US company sets up a fresh factory as its first step.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory; it is the growing kind, and 'to begin with' makes the acorn its start.
annotation.definitionFit: An acorn is what an oak starts as, a plant at its beginning.

entries.clue: Issue demanding answer for leader’s wealth (9)

indicators.note: the word asks for A to be put in
A goes in place of the first letter

blocks.note: effluence = something that flows out, an issue
a = answer; it replaces the leading E

annotation.surface: A pressing question about why the man at the top is so rich.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a topic; it is an outflow, as a river issues.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: affluence, literally a flowing towards, came to mean a plentiful supply of money.

entries.clue: Unsatisfactory compromise that’s annoying! (5)

blocks.note: a botched deal that dodges the real issue, as politicians make
a mild exclamation, a polite stand-in for a swear word

annotation.surface: Someone exasperated by a half-baked deal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fudge!' is a mild exclamation of irritation, a polite substitute for a swear word.
annotation.definitionFit: A fudge is a botched compromise, and 'fudge!' is said when something annoys.

entries.clue: Vulnerable individual recruited for experiment (7)

blocks.note: the adjective meaning liable or exposed, followed by 'to'
the person a trial or study is carried out on

annotation.surface: A fragile person signed up for a trial.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is the adjective, as in 'subject to attack'.
annotation.definitionFit: Subject means liable or exposed to something, and a subject is a person tested in an experiment.

entries.clue: Cadet is shaped and moulded (3-4)

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new shape

annotation.surface: A young recruit being licked into shape by training.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shaped and moulded' look like a pair of synonyms; one is the indicator, the other the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Die-cast means made by forcing molten metal into a mould.

entries.clue: One with no chance of success is sweet? (10)

definitions.text: One with no chance of success

annotation.surface: A hopeless candidate turns out to be rather endearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as charming; it is the pudding, which at a meal is not a starter (a first course).
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a hopeless prospect, and a joke: the sweet course comes last, so it is literally not the starter.

blocks.clueFragment: One with no chance of success
blocks.note: an idea or candidate that is going nowhere
a sweet (pudding) is eaten last, so it is not a starter course

entries.clue: Acknowledgements of liabilities ignored by painstaking boss (4)

indicators.note: IOUS is left out of STUDIOUS

blocks.note: IOUs acknowledge debts; they are removed

annotation.surface: A careful manager who never looks at the debts on the books.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager; it is a raised knob, as on a shield.
annotation.definitionFit: A boss is a round raised stud or knob.
